Forecast Discussion

High pressure over Quebec and a storm parked a few hundred miles off the Delmarva coast hold the pattern in place. Troughs sit east and west of us with a ridge over the middle of the country, and nothing moves much for a week. The air stays dry, and dry air cools fast at night and warms fast by day. The cooler air sinks into valleys at night, producing huge temperature differences bottom to top, and the dry air warms quickly again to a pleasant afternoon.

Wednesday and Thursday aren’t copies of Tuesday, but they do rhyme.

A reinforcement knocks at the door Friday. A new high settles over Pennsylvania and New York Friday night and noses down the east side of the mountains. The weekend is noticeably cooler but not uncomfortable for fall. You may not shed the sweater as quickly those days.

The high settles over the Carolinas Monday, and afternoons warm into the start of next week.

Rain? The pattern does not break before the end of October. The first rain of any consequence waits for early November.
